card.name: Lambada
card.tagline: Para-origin couples dance, a 1989 global sensation.
card.profile: Lambada is a partner dance (and music genre) originating in Para, northern Brazil, fusing carimbo with Caribbean and other rhythms. Danced in close embrace with pronounced hip movement and arched turns, often with short skirts and circular motion, it became a worldwide craze in 1989 via Kaoma's single 'Lambada' (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: Kaoma's 'Lambada' (1989) sold millions worldwide and topped charts in over 15 countries; per English Wikipedia it was the most successful European single in the history of CBS Records. Lambada is the direct parent of Brazilian Zouk.

steps.name: The Basic
steps.description: Step side to side with bent knees and loose hips

steps.name: The Side Sit
steps.description: Lady sits on partner's leg while moving side to side

steps.name: The Turn
steps.description: Lady turns while always facing the partner

steps.name: The Dip
steps.description: Partner holds lady securely around the waist and dips her back

safety: Hold your partner strongly with your arms around the lady so you can let her go with no fear
lessons.teacher_style: The instructors break down the dance into numbered steps, demonstrating both individually and together. They maintain an encouraging, playful tone throughout the lesson.
lessons.distinctive_method: Breaking down partner dancing by first showing individual solo footwork and upper body posture before combining into partner hold.
what_works: Demonstrating solo then with a partner
